
Scanned arXiv RSS signals from 2026-06-29. Two papers stand out as strong candidates: one on symbolic feedback-driven iterative self-refinement for LLM planning, and one on parameterized world models reducing hallucination propagation in LLM agents. Both address architectural patterns, tool-use/execution design, and iterative refinement with empirical grounding. The Grok social signals reference URLs that are either non-existent or already covered (Anthropic building-effective-agents is already in the README). Other arXiv entries are domain-specific (dyslexia, emotion recognition, KG completion) or lack agentic workflow design focus.

## Suggestions

- [Towards Reliable and Robust LLM Planning: Symbolic Feedback-Driven Iterative Self-Refinement Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27757) — Proposes a symbolic feedback-driven iterative self-refinement framework for LLM planning, addressing reliability, recovery loops, and structured evaluation feedback across agent execution stages.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability)

- [Grounded Iterative Language Planning: How Parameterized World Models Reduce Hallucination Propagation in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27806) — Introduces grounded iterative language planning with parameterized world models to reduce hallucination propagation in LLM agents, with empirical analysis of planning reliability across multi-step agentic tasks.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)
